channels.title: Mike Callahan's Firehouse
channels.description:
Hi, I'm Mike Callahan, a retired firefighter, and I show you how to make sure your house never makes the 911 call.

Whether you're a homeowner, you live alone, or you're looking out for parents who do, you're in the right place. For twenty-eight years I walked through what was left of people's homes the morning after — and it was almost never something exotic. It was the dryer, the space heater, the extension cord, the pan on the stove.

Here you'll learn what really starts house fires — the lint line, the power strip, the battery charging by the door — how to remove each risk in minutes for free, and how to make sure your smoke alarms will actually wake you when it counts. No scare tactics, no gadgets to buy. Just the checks firefighters run in their own homes.

New videos every week to keep your family safe and the fire trucks off your street.

Subscribe if you'd rather prevent it than survive it.

channels.title: Triple J Fire
channels.description:
Videos of FDNY, NYPD, and EMS responding in NYC, along with occasional emergency and other interesting vehicles elsewhere.
Call me an accidental fire buff. My now 9-year-old son became fascinated by the FDNY as a toddler. I started recording videos just for him. Then I started trying to frame the vehicles up nicely and found myself getting excited when we found new units.  It expanded exponentially when we started listening to Manhattan dispatch radio all day and going to anything we could reasonably and safely watch. 
But I've really been interested forever. Growing up, I remember the excitement of hearing the beeps and static of fire radios during holiday dinners as my grandfather and two uncles were volunteer firefighters, and they'd race out to calls. I can thank my son for reinvigorating my interest! Now, I also hope having this channel helps to honor my late grandfather's incredible 73 years of volunteer fire service.

channels.title: Konrad Fischer's Woodfire
channels.description:
My name is Konrad Fischer. I have heated my house with wood for forty years in the Black Forest, and my father did the same before me.

In Germany we do not treat wood heat as a hobby. Firewood is seasoned two years, not one. A chimney sweep inspects every stove by law. Nobody burns wet wood, because everyone was taught what wet wood does to a flue.

Most people I meet who burn wood are doing three or four things wrong that nobody ever corrected. Not because they are careless — because nobody told them. That is what this channel is for.

Every week: which woods to burn and which to never put in a stove, how to season firewood properly, how to run a stove so it holds heat all night, and how to keep a chimney safe.

Everything here comes from forty years of doing it, not from a manual.
